prompt.brief: Design a cost-efficient e-commerce backend that handles catalog browsing, inventory, checkout, payments, fulfillment, and traffic spikes while preserving order correctness.
successSignals: Define catalog, inventory reservation, cart, order, payment, shipment, and return boundaries with idempotent state transitions.
Keep browse reads highly cacheable while making checkout strongly correct around stock, totals, payment authorization, and order creation.
Design for flash-sale bursts, hot products, asynchronous fulfillment, payment webhooks, retries, reconciliation, and dead-letter recovery.
Explain security, fraud controls, observability, cost guardrails, and degraded browsing or checkout behavior.

functional: Browse and search products, manage carts, reserve inventory, create orders, authorize/capture/refund payments, and track fulfillment.
Support authenticated customers, guest checkout, promotions, tax/shipping quotes, seller/admin updates, and order history.
Make retries safe, reconcile payment and inventory mismatches, audit sensitive actions, and recover from partial workflow failures.
nonFunctional: Meet p95 browse latency under 200ms and checkout confirmation under 2 seconds excluding external payment latency.
Scale from quiet periods to 100x flash-sale bursts without a single hot key or unbounded synchronous work.
Do not lose committed state; make retries and duplicate events safe.
Degrade safely when downstream workers, caches, or external dependencies fail.
scaleAssumptions: 100x traffic bursts; 50k checkout attempts per minute
Partition by the primary tenant, user, item, or geographic key and isolate hot partitions.
Keep serving state bounded; retain raw events or durable records for replay and auditing.

architecture.title: Scalable E Commerce Backend domain architecture
architecture.summary: Design a cost-efficient e-commerce backend that handles catalog browsing, inventory, checkout, payments, fulfillment, and traffic spikes while preserving order correctness. The design makes scalable e commerce backend decisions durable, isolates slow or external work behind replayable boundaries, and exposes freshness, authorization, and recovery state to operators and clients.

layers.label: Shopper and catalog plane
layers.description: Browse, search, eligibility, and checkout requests enter through the protected API.

layers.label: Commerce and order truth
layers.description: Inventory claims and order transitions are versioned and conditionally committed.

layers.label: Payment and fulfillment plane
layers.description: External payment and slow fulfillment work are replayable and bounded.

layers.label: Customer status plane
layers.description: Order and delivery status is delivered independently from the commit path.

layers.label: Commerce reliability operations
layers.description: Hot inventory, bot traffic, payment, and backlog signals protect the promise.

deepDives.title: Inventory claims and oversell control
points: Use conditional writes or a serialized inventory partition for scalable e commerce backend scarce capacity.
Give holds an expiry and reaper, but never release a confirmed claim from a stale worker.
Separate searchable availability from the authoritative claim path.

deepDives.title: Payment and unknown outcomes
points: Bind scalable e commerce backend payment attempts to the intent and request hash, not just the customer session.
Treat timeout as unknown, query or reconcile provider state, and avoid a blind second charge.
Keep sensitive payment tokens outside business records and logs.

deepDives.title: Fulfillment and partner recovery
points: Publish scalable e commerce backend events after commit, consume at least once, and track per-stage progress.
Use reconciliation against partner feeds or delivery evidence instead of assuming a callback arrives.
Expose pending and expired status so the client can explain what happened.

tradeoffs.title: Reservation versus oversell tolerance
tradeoffs.recommendation: Prefer a short-lived scalable e commerce backend claim for scarce inventory and state the consistency scope explicitly.
tradeoffs.caution: A cache or search index cannot safely decrement the final stock count.

tradeoffs.title: Synchronous checkout versus asynchronous fulfillment
tradeoffs.recommendation: Commit the order intent synchronously and move partner or delivery work behind events.
tradeoffs.caution: Waiting for downstream fulfillment makes retries ambiguous and increases checkout tail latency.

tradeoffs.title: Precompute availability versus compute at read time
tradeoffs.recommendation: Precompute common search dimensions but validate the final claim against authoritative state.
tradeoffs.caution: Serving only a precomputed scalable e commerce backend availability view creates oversell or stale-price failures.

commonMistakes: Charging before a scalable e commerce backend inventory claim is durable.
Retrying a timed-out payment without resolving the first attempt.
Letting stale search results act as the final availability decision.
Making cancellation and hold expiry non-idempotent.
Failing to reconcile late partner confirmations, refunds, or delivery failures.

followUps.question: How do you avoid double orders?
followUps.answer: Persist the scalable e commerce backend request idempotency key, condition the intent transition, and make inventory, payment, and fulfillment consumers deduplicate the same command.

followUps.question: What if inventory changes between search and checkout?
followUps.answer: Recheck authoritative availability, return an explicit unavailable or repriced result, and do not silently convert a failed claim into a confirmed one.

followUps.question: How do you repair a stuck fulfillment?
followUps.answer: Use an operation timeline, provider evidence, retry-safe transitions, and an operator-approved compensating action or cancellation.

rubric.description: The answer addresses the scalable e commerce backend workflow, scale, latency, durability, authorization, and failure contract.
The answer identifies the authoritative scalable e commerce backend state, versioning or deduplication boundary, and how derived views converge.
The answer partitions scalable e commerce backend traffic, isolates hot keys, and moves fan-out, retries, or rebuilds behind bounded asynchronous work.
The answer names freshness, backlog, error, cost, and recovery signals tied to the scalable e commerce backend user experience.
